title: Append is associative over a computed List
statement: For any three lists a, b, c over a common element type, appending (a then b) then c gives the same list as appending a then (b then c) -- List.append is associative.

formal.statement: ((x0 : Sort (1)) -> ((x1 : List.{0} x0) -> ((x2 : List.{0} x0) -> ((x3 : List.{0} x0) -> Eq.{1} (List.{0} x0) (List.append x0 (List.append x0 x1 x2) x3) (List.append x0 x1 (List.append x0 x2 x3))))))

evidence.supports: List.append_assoc is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement.
evidence.checker_command: test "$(cargo run -q --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example list_theorem_inventory -- List.append_assoc 2>/dev/null | grep -Fc '((x0 : Sort (1)) -> ((x1 : List.{0} x0) -> ((x2 : List.{0} x0) -> ((x3 : List.{0} x0) -> Eq.{1} (List.{0} x0) (List.append x0 (List.append x0 x1 x2) x3) (List.append x0 x1 (List.append x0 x2 x3))))))')" -ge 1

notes: Both nil case (Eq.refl, since both sides collapse to `append l2 l3` by iota alone) and cons case (congr on `cons head _` through the induction hypothesis) are ordinary List.rec inductions; no equation lemma was needed because List.append recurses on its FIRST argument.
